thread:
mei: quick heads-up — ran a narrow perf pass on the host path for the new batch routing changes. seeing ~48% host CPU in request parsing/tokenization and another ~22% blocked in grpc writev syscall during streaming bursts. sample pprof attached but TL;DR: parsing + chunking >> kernel time on short-seq workloads.

arjun: +1, saw this on canary around 7151234000. kernel selection looks fine but we waste time before we even pick a kernel.

sam: is the tokenizer single-threaded per request? that sounds high.

mei: yes, current host tokenizer is lock-per-connection single-threaded. most requests are tiny (seq < 64) but we still do full UTF8 normalization + regex header checks.

jess: that regex header check is suspicious — we patched it in 2023 to be strict. can we relax for known-service clients? maybe short-circuit.

mei: proof point from pprof:
```
(pprof) top
Showing nodes accounting for 1.23s, 90% of 1.36s total
      flat  flat%   sum%        cum   cum%
     0.42s 30.9% 30.9%      0.42s 30.9%  runtime.regexMatch
     0.30s 22.1% 53.0%      0.72s 52.9%  grpc.(*Server).handleWritev
     0.18s 13.2% 66.2%      0.18s 13.2%  tokenizer.normalize
     0.12s  8.8% 75.0%      0.30s 22.1%  host.parseRequest
```

mei: so regex + normalize + parseRequest are the bulk on host. grpc writev shows up because we flush lots of small chunks.

arjun: ok. two-pronged: (1) preparse gating — detect short requests by raw content-length and skip heavy normalize/regex for known ok clients, (2) chunk coalescing in proxy before writev to reduce syscall tail.

sam: for (1) we can add a fast-path in the front of host-proxy: if len(payload) < 128 && header X-Client-Type in {runt, sdk} then skip full-normalize. cheap check.

jess: for kernel selection, if we get a microsecond-level preparse, we can pick a kernel earlier. but most current heuristics only run after tokenization which delays selection. maybe run a lightweight kernel-suggestor on raw-length + prompt-type.

mei: I prototyped a suggestor:
```
// pseudo
if raw_tokens_estimate <= 64 {
  prefer kernel = "fast_small_seq";
} else if quantized && seq <= 512 {
  prefer kernel = "int8_grouped";
} else {
  prefer kernel = "fp16_default";
}
```
it reduces decision latency by ~200us in local bench.

arjun: nice. also KV cache thrash note: when we coalesce chunks in gateway, we reduced duplicate KV lookups. without coalesce we were filling the KV cache with many short-lived prefixes (hotset churn).

mei: yes — pprof also showed a lot of time in kvcache.lookup for small prefixes during bursts: it correlates with high eviction rate and more cache misses.

sam: actionables?

mei: propose:
- RFC small-path: implement X-Client-Type quick check to skip regex/normalize for payload < 128 (canary in gateway).
- Coalesce enum: gateway should aggregate writes until either 4KB or 5ms then single writev. default 1ms is too aggressive.
- Kernel-suggestor: move heuristic earlier to pre-tokenize stage; expose as opt-in flag.
- KV tuning: increase per-shard small-prefix TTL and add rate limiter on repeated prefix lookups from same client.

arjun: sounds good. canary plan?

deploy-bot: canary created by @mei -> service/host-proxy:v2026-7151234600 at 7151234600 :rocket:

jess: test plan — perf harness: 10k tiny requests/s for 60s with and without coalesce, measure p95 parse latency and grpc syscall count. also run model bench to ensure kernel selection unchanged for medium/large seq.

sam: I'll add the quick-check patch and coalesce config toggle behind feature-flag. target PRs today.

infra-bot: added perf tracepoint hooks to host-proxy at /metrics: host_parse_fastpath_count, host_writev_coalesce_count, kvcache_evictions_smallprefix.

mei: awesome. if we get ~30-40% parse reduction and 50% fewer writev syscalls p95 we should recover most of the host-side overhead and let kernels dominate again.

arjun: rough rollback criteria: if p95 increases or errors > 0.1% on canary, revert.

jess: will run the benches once canary is warm. thanks folks, keep updates here. :thumbsup:
